I wrote a review of the new Star Wars soundtrack. Should I keep this up?

A good soundtrack is a lot like a good janitor. When the janitor is doing his job well, nobody really says anything about him - instead, everyone comments on what a great building it is. It's only when he does a bad job that anyone pays him any mind. The thing with most movie soundtracks (especially those that use big orchestral arrangements) where the scores were designed specifically for the movie is that the music is almost never meant to be heard apart from the movie.

Star Wars music is such that I would never want to listen to it in my car - that's like eating a big bowl of butter and salt without any popcorn. On the other hand, I couldn't imagine wanting star wars movies to be without it. In my opinion, star wars music doesn't adequately stand on its own - but it shines when it's working along side the material for which it was intended. I don't think it makes much sense to review the music separate from the movie.

I've been in LOTS of fights. I'll just point out some highlights. (Editor's note, this was years ago, I'm married with kids now, no fights for me!!)

I have always had a loud mouth and attracted a lot of attention, both good and bad. When you have that quality, you are going to run into somebody at some point who is going to want to get physical for one of the two, and frankly, more often the good. If you have the gift of gab and you're getting attention from the opposite sex, at some point somebody's going to resent you enough to try to shut your mouth with a solid fist to it.

I've been jumped by a gang of Chicanos in Long Beach, had my collar bone broken by a Judo master, been beaten mercilessly by a group of cops (for no fucking reason, as usual), and put another guy in the hospital with internal hemorrhaging. I didn't start any of these fights, directly, but as I said before when you've got a big yapper, you're gonna run afoul of someone eventually.

I had quite a temper myself when I was younger, so to curb that I did martial arts at a young age. This helped immensely, both in being able to defend myself (short of groups and superior martial artists, sadly), and in being able to control my own temper.

MOST of the fights I can recall were over a girl, and in all but one case a girl I had little or no interest or history with. This scenario generally makes it easy to win the fight. When someone else is enraged, and you are calm, you instantly have the upper hand, size and other factors seem secondary, frankly. I ended up successfully evading the gang that probably would have killed me in Long Beach long enough to make a break for it and run for my life, but mainly because I was calm, and they were angry. Over some trollip that I had zero involvement in, as usual. The first dude to swing on me swung with all his might, clumsily, missed me altogether, and then spun half way around knocking into one of his homies (not hard, but enough for me to make a break for it, and I was a good runner back then).

The fight where I hospitalized the guy, was not my fault at all. Again it was over some girl that I barely knew, but found out later she had been talking about me to a few people and this guy that liked her must have overheard. Fast forward a month or two, I'm at a party and have had a couple of drinks. I was tall, but super skinny (at the time, I was probably 17-18?). This dude was shorter than me, but ALL muscle, and was a boxer in the navy. Any way, I'm at this party, and dude shows up and starts hollering about beating me to death out in front of the house. I didn't hear or know what was happening, or I'd probably have stayed hidden in the back. But I heard some commotion and came to investigate. Big mistake. The girl who's house it was (friend of mine and the dude, but not the girl he was interested in. I don't think. I never really got the full story there, actually) was trying to cool him down and keep him out of her house. He caught sight of me coming to investigate the commotion, and the bull was loose!

Now, at the time, as I said, I'd been drinking, and this guy looked sober, and MAD, and he was FUCKING RIPPED, and a bit older than me, and routinely fought in the ring. I was scared shitless. But even so, I'd probably have danced around or ran for it, except storming past the girl who's house it was, he took her down. I'm sure it was an accident, but I didn't wait to find out, and at this point we're looking at a home invasion scenario, and I didn't really have time or room to evade or run. So I put everything I had in a round house kick square to the gut while she was still in a downward motion. At the time I was in a Tae Kwon Do class, and was clocked on the meter at over 1600 ppsi (pounds per square inch) pretty regularly (I'm 6' 3" and had training). Now that's "in the lab", and this was in an entry way drunk at a party, but I was also pretty much in fight or flight mode, so I'm sure my adrenaline was giving me an extra boost.

The guy went down immediately, and his friends immediately carried him to a car and peeled out. I think they realized it was a aggravated home invasion charge if the cops showed up, so they were covering their own asses. I heard later he had very significant injuries and was trying to get me for a doctor's bill. I politely told the mutual friend that I was sorry for his suffering and bills, but that he was aggressively entering the home of someone against their will, and had already knocked down a young woman.

Anyway, I think from that moment on I've pulled my punches a little bit no matter the scenario. It's not an easy burden knowing you have probably shortened someone's lifetime just because they had a temper at some dumb party. My son is getting tall now, and I try very hard every day to instill that fear of hurting someone in him, but unfortunately it seems like it might be one of those lessons you have to learn on your own. Or maybe I'm a lousy teacher. Dunno.

The moral of my story(s) here is this: Do NOT glamorize fights or fighting. There is a real potential to do real harm, even in a scenario wherein you are not the instigator, and evading or escaping is always the best outcome for everyone. It's not cowardice. It's fucking smart. Be fucking smart.

I've been in LOTS of fights. I'll just point out some highlights. (Editor's note, this was years ago, I'm married with kids now, no fights for me!!)

I have always had a loud mouth and attracted a lot of attention, both good and bad. When you have that quality, you are going to run into somebody at some point who is going to want to get physical for one of the two, and frankly, more often the good. If you have the gift of gab and you're getting attention from the opposite sex, at some point somebody's going to resent you enough to try to shut your mouth with a solid fist to it.

I've been jumped by a gang of Chicanos in Long Beach, had my collar bone broken by a Judo master, been beaten mercilessly by a group of cops (for no fucking reason, as usual), and put another guy in the hospital with internal hemorrhaging. I didn't start any of these fights, directly, but as I said before when you've got a big yapper, you're gonna run afoul of someone eventually.

I had quite a temper myself when I was younger, so to curb that I did martial arts at a young age. This helped immensely, both in being able to defend myself (short of groups and superior martial artists, sadly), and in being able to control my own temper.

MOST of the fights I can recall were over a girl, and in all but one case a girl I had little or no interest or history with. This scenario generally makes it easy to win the fight. When someone else is enraged, and you are calm, you instantly have the upper hand, size and other factors seem secondary, frankly. I ended up successfully evading the gang that probably would have killed me in Long Beach long enough to make a break for it and run for my life, but mainly because I was calm, and they were angry. Over some trollip that I had zero involvement in, as usual. The first dude to swing on me swung with all his might, clumsily, missed me altogether, and then spun half way around knocking into one of his homies (not hard, but enough for me to make a break for it, and I was a good runner back then).

The fight where I hospitalized the guy, was not my fault at all. Again it was over some girl that I barely knew, but found out later she had been talking about me to a few people and this guy that liked her must have overheard. Fast forward a month or two, I'm at a party and have had a couple of drinks. I was tall, but super skinny (at the time, I was probably 17-18?). This dude was shorter than me, but ALL muscle, and was a boxer in the navy. Any way, I'm at this party, and dude shows up and starts hollering about beating me to death out in front of the house. I didn't hear or know what was happening, or I'd probably have stayed hidden in the back. But I heard some commotion and came to investigate. Big mistake. The girl who's house it was (friend of mine and the dude, but not the girl he was interested in. I don't think. I never really got the full story there, actually) was trying to cool him down and keep him out of her house. He caught sight of me coming to investigate the commotion, and the bull was loose!

Now, at the time, as I said, I'd been drinking, and this guy looked sober, and MAD, and he was FUCKING RIPPED, and a bit older than me, and routinely fought in the ring. I was scared shitless. But even so, I'd probably have danced around or ran for it, except storming past the girl who's house it was, he took her down. I'm sure it was an accident, but I didn't wait to find out, and at this point we're looking at a home invasion scenario, and I didn't really have time or room to evade or run. So I put everything I had in a round house kick square to the gut while she was still in a downward motion. At the time I was in a Tae Kwon Do class, and was clocked on the meter at over 1600 ppsi (pounds per square inch) pretty regularly (I'm 6' 3" and had training). Now that's "in the lab", and this was in an entry way drunk at a party, but I was also pretty much in fight or flight mode, so I'm sure my adrenaline was giving me an extra boost.
